content.user_title: Manage Git History, Conflicts, and Recovery
content.value_statement: Unclear commits, conflicting branches, and lost changes can slow repository work. This skill guides focused commits, history inspection, conflict resolution, and recovery using established Git practices.
actual_capabilities: Guides selective staging and Conventional Commits messages for focused changes.
Explains feature branches, merge choices, and private-history rebasing.
Suggests status, diff, log, blame, and bisect for repository inspection.
Explains restore, amend, revert, reset, stash, and reflog recovery options.
Guides conflict resolution with behavior checks, builds, tests, and optional rerere.
Recommends branch protection, signed commits, annotated tags, and secret prevention.
limitations: Provides written guidance, not a standalone Git implementation or automated recovery system.
Command execution requires Git, repository access, and an assistant with terminal permissions.
Reflog recovery depends on retained objects and does not guarantee recovery of uncommitted changes.
Does not configure hosting policies, signing keys, or secret-scanning hooks automatically.

use_cases.title: Prepare focused commits
use_cases.description: Separate unrelated changes and draft consistent commit messages before opening a pull request.

use_cases.title: Coordinate branch integration
use_cases.description: Choose merge or rebase strategies while preserving shared history and validating conflict resolutions.

use_cases.title: Investigate regressions and recovery
use_cases.description: Trace changes with history tools, plan bisect checks, and identify recovery options for misplaced commits.

prompt_templates.title: Inspect repository changes
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect my repository status and diffs. Summarize staged and unstaged changes without modifying files or history.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: understand the current working state.

prompt_templates.title: Plan focused commits
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my changes and propose separate logical commits with Conventional Commits messages. Wait for approval before staging or committing.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: prepare a clear contribution history.

prompt_templates.title: Resolve branch conflicts
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect conflicts between [feature branch] and [target branch]. Propose resolutions that preserve intended behavior and identify tests before continuing integration.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: integrate changes without losing behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Investigate a lost commit
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect status, log, and reflog to locate [lost change]. Explain recovery options and risks; request approval before any reset or history rewrite.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: recover history while protecting current work.

output_examples.input: I changed login behavior and corrected documentation. How should I organize the commits?
output: Separate the login change from the documentation correction.
Stage each logical change selectively and verify the staged diff.
Use a feature commit for login behavior and a documentation commit for the correction.
Run relevant tests before committing the behavior change.

output_examples.input: A bad commit is already on a shared branch. What is the appropriate undo strategy?
output: Prefer a revert that adds an inverse commit and preserves shared history.
Inspect later changes for dependencies and check for conflicts.
Validate the resulting behavior before publishing the revert.
Avoid resetting or force-pushing the shared branch.

output_examples.input: I cannot find a commit after moving my branch. How should I investigate?
output: Inspect the reflog for the previous branch position.
Confirm that the candidate commit contains the expected changes.
Protect current work before choosing a recovery operation.
Recovery may fail if the required Git objects are no longer retained.

best_practices: Inspect status and diffs, then obtain explicit approval before discarding changes or rewriting history.
Keep commits focused and validate behavior with builds and tests after resolving conflicts.
Preserve shared history and follow repository review, branch protection, and deployment policies.
anti_patterns: Using hard reset or file restore without checking and protecting uncommitted work.
Rebasing or force-pushing branches that other contributors depend on.
Accepting every conflict from one side without reviewing intended behavior or running tests.

faq.question: Which assistants are supported?
faq.answer: The skill lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code. Running Git commands depends on the assistant environment and granted permissions.

faq.question: Does the skill include executable scripts?
faq.answer: No. The reviewed package contains one Markdown instruction file with Git examples and workflow guidance.

faq.question: Does it require a paid service?
faq.answer: The skill specifies no paid service dependency. Your assistant or repository hosting provider may have separate costs.

faq.question: Should I rebase a shared branch?
faq.answer: The guidance prohibits rewriting history that others depend on. Rebase private work and preserve shared history through the agreed repository workflow.

faq.question: Can it recover every lost change?
faq.answer: No. Reflog can help locate retained commits, but discarded uncommitted changes and removed objects may not be recoverable.

faq.question: How does it reduce accidental secret exposure?
faq.answer: It advises against committing secrets and recommends ignore rules plus optional secret scanning. These suggestions do not replace dedicated scanning or review.
